2.text: Wuˊthɪtčä-čaˊkêt-tɵˊmg̣ɪn (“middle sister-mate”) Middle sister (said by female).

3.text: Ñêˊnča-čaˊkêt-tɵˊmg̣ɪn (“younger sister-mate”). Younger sister (said by female).

5.text: Yêᵋˊlo Male cousin, paternal and maternal.

6.text: Ñaw-yêᵋˊlhɪ-tɵˊmg̣ɪn (in respect to male cousins)¹ Female cousin, paternal and maternal.

13.text: Of all these terms, a collective may be formed by means of the word

14.text: -ret, -rat, which signifies “collection,” “set,” and is used only in combination

15.text: with others. Thus, yičemreˊt, “company of brothers;” čakêˊttɪrat, “company

16.text: of sisters” (in regard to the male relatives); yêᵋˊlhɪrat, “company of male

17.text: cousins;” kret, “company of boys” (k shortened for kmiˊñɪn, “boy,” “child”).

18.text: The fourth degree of relationship is designated by means of the stem

20.text: yɪlh-ᴇʟuˊê, “great-grandson;” yɪlhɪʟoˊo-tɵˊmg̣ɪn, “male cousin twice removed,” etc.

21.text: The more remote degrees of relationship are designated as čɪmčeˊkin,

22.text: “the near one;” or čičeˊtkin, čičeˊʟeñ, “kinsman.” The compass of the second

23.text: term is larger than that of the first.

24.text: All degrees of step-relations are designated with the suffix -lqäl, meaning

25.text: “intended for.”⁴ Thus ᴇʟɪˊhɪlqäl, “step-father;” ᴇʟaˊlqäl, step-mother,” also,

26.text: in polygamous families, “another wife of my father;” eˊkkelqäl, “step-son;”

28.text: “step-sister” (in repect to the brother), etc. Even ñew-miˊrg̣ɪlqäl, “step-grand-

29.text: mother,” is often used in polygamous families.

41.text: Ñeumiˊrit (“woman umiˊrit”) Son-in-law’s or daughter-in-law’s mother.

42.text: ¹ Women use the term ñawˊg̣êl, which is the female pronunciation of ñaw-yêᵋˊlhɪ.

43.text: ² Female pronunciation, ᴇʟuˊwg̣o-tɵˊmg̣ɪn. ᴇʟoo and ᴇʟuˊe are related.

44.text: ³ Female pronunciation, ñauʟuˊwg̣o-tɵˊmg̣ɪn. Women among themselves use simply the term ñawˊg̣êl.

45.text: ⁴ For instance, uwäˊᵋqučilqäl (“intended for husband”), “bridegroom;” ñeˊwänlɪqäl (“intended for wife”), “bride.”

46.text: ⁵ From the verb mataˊrkɪn (“thou takest,” “thou takest to wife”).

47.text: ⁶ Aaˊčêk means “young man;” ñeˊus˙qät means “woman.” These terms are used by both wedded parties.

48.text: Sometimes they say also ᴇndêw-mataˊlɪn (“wife’s uncle”) and ᴇččaiˊñaw-mataˊlɪn (“wife’s aunt”).
